promotion_note: PROMOTED 2026-07-28 (owner sign-off this session — "if structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper" — on the standing 'structurally more accurate = new keeper' standard, rule 1 [R-STRUCT]): ERCOT keeper -> 2026-07-28-ercot129-conditional-coal-min (bundle results/calibration/ercot129_conditional) — the 2026-07-26-ercot115-coal-marginal-hr recipe with a SINGLE delta, ercot_coal_min_config_floor armed. THE MECHANISM: a coal plant may not be pushed below the registered minimum load of its SMALLEST ONLINE CONFIGURATION, min over its units of the EIA-860 'Minimum Load (MW)' (10 plants / 13,611 MW / 2,164 MW total, cap-weighted 0.1590; data/raw/_processed-legacy/coal_min_config_ERCOT.csv, scripts/data/derive_eia860_coal_min_config.py). It REMOVES A STRUCTURAL FALSEHOOD rather than closing a residual: the LP carries one variable per plant with no lower bound, so it was driving coal to levels no combination of that plant's units can physically deliver (outgoing keeper per-plant p05 loading 0.013-0.093 of declared against a real fleet whose floor is 0.106-0.261). Applied AVAILABILITY-CONDITIONALLY — the plant delivers its whole minimum configuration or nothing, because a minimum online configuration does not shrink when units go out — with the level re-allocated across the plant's coal tranches in fill order on their AVAILABLE capacity each hour. NO INTEGRALITY AND NO MIP: availability is exogenous data, not a decision variable, and the plant's exact unit-commitment feasible set is the connected interval [min_u MinLoad_u, Cap] for 9 of 10 plants and 97.76% of ERCOT coal capacity, so the plant-grain bound represents unit-grain commitment's lower envelope with ZERO relaxation error there (Major Oak, 305 MW, is a strict relaxation and is recorded as such in the artifact's `connected` column). STRUCTURAL RESULT (the win condition, pre-registered as G7): physically-impossible online plant-hours — plant online but below its own min_u MinLoad_u — fall 14,582 -> 2,074 (2023), 13,020 -> 3,262 (2024), 9,558 -> 1,240 (2025), i.e. 85.8 / 74.9 / 87.0 % against the outgoing keeper and 18.7 -> 2.6 / 17.0 -> 4.2 / 13.1 -> 1.7 % as a share of online hours. Per-plant p05 loading moves TOWARD the real fleet in 22 of 29 plant-years (the availability-SCALED control managed 10 of 29). ZERO DOF COST (rule 21): DOF ledger 10 -> 11 entries with the RESIDUAL count UNCHANGED at 8 — the new entry is measured-physical with lineage_solves 0, carrying 0 free scalars, and offer_curve_by_group is untouched at 111. The derive reads one registration file and takes a minimum, so it has no residual input by construction (rule 23). Corroborated on an independent filing: the ERCOT COP LSL agrees EXACTLY on the three plants whose resources are whole units (Coleto Creek 175, Oak Grove 348, J K Spruce 130). PRE-COMMITTED 8/8 PASS (PRECOMMIT-ercot129-coal-minconfig-conditional-2026-07-28.md, written and pushed BEFORE the solve): G0 arming+bite (3/3 ARMED lines, run_config carries the flag, D-2 coal_min_config 3.198/2.872/2.546 TWh); G1 loading-vs-price 19/21 = the outgoing keeper's 19/21 (do-no-harm — it FIXES 2023 <$15, 0.488 -> 0.507 vs 0.552 actual, and breaks 2024 >=$50, 0.765 -> 0.771 vs 0.720); G2 C1 coal +0.371 / +0.797 / -1.167 TWh against the keeper's -1.078 / -0.294 / -1.926, all inside +-2.0 and BETTER on mean absolute (0.78 vs 1.10); G3 D-1 no coal class-year flips pass->fail (2023 COAL_LIGNITE remains the outgoing keeper's own FAIL, 0.745/0.294 -> 0.710/0.288); G4 C1 all 16/16 free 12/12 with coal forced share 5.26/4.92/4.17 % against the 30 % cap; G5 LOYO (one of three years shows a G1 regression, not two); G6 DOF as above; G7 as above. D-4 coal_min_config off-window share 0.0 % in all three years (window h0-23, all hours BY DRIVER). RUBRIC PROFILE IS IDENTICAL to the outgoing keeper: C1 / C2 / C4 / C8 PASS, C3a / C3b / C3c / C7 FAIL, C6 UNATTESTED. DETERMINATION REMAINS NOT-YET — NOT calibrated. C6 stays UNATTESTED DELIBERATELY and like-for-like: the gate requires asserting levers_trace_to_measured_input, still FALSE while 8 residual-identified DOF entries remain, exactly as for the outgoing keeper. PRICE COST ON THE RECORD (declared, and NOT counted for the mechanism, rule 1): C3a DEGRADES marginally in every year — 2023 -26.9 -> -27.2 %, 2024 -13.1 -> -13.4 %, 2025 -0.8 -> -1.1 % — about 0.3 pp, with the FAIL/PASS profile unchanged. TWO p05 OVERSHOOTS ON THE RECORD: Oak Grove 2023 (actual 0.467) is PRE-EXISTING and REDUCED, 0.767 -> 0.690; San Miguel 2025 is NEW, 0.493 -> 0.639 against actual 0.585, a +0.054 overshoot on a 391 MW single-unit plant (2.9 % of ERCOT coal capacity) whose registered minimum load is genuinely 0.639 of its capacity — reality occasionally runs it below its own filed LSL, which is a question about that plant's registration, not evidence the mechanism is wrong. Open, not hidden. ALSO STILL OPEN: 7.4 / 11.6 / 0.0 % of the original impossible plant-hours sit at plants that cannot reach min_config at all in that hour; those need an UPPER bound (cap the plant off), which is a separate leg and is NOT built here. D-4 reliability_floor x CT_PEAKER still FAILs off-window: PRE-EXISTING and unchanged. Prior frontier/lineage note follows. --- FRONTIER WITHDRAWN — ERCOT reverts to NOT-YET (owner directive 2026-07-17, the ERCOT-79 availability-envelope audit: 'we can't have a keeper on inaccurate data'). The 2026-07-17 frontier declaration rested on a keeper (ercot76) whose scarcity tail was formed on a PHANTOM CAMPD facility-outage bug: the run-based detector hard-zeroed ~1.9-5.7 GW of daily-cycling combined-cycle capability its own CEMS shows generating (T H Wharton et al.), artificially exhausting the event-time fleet so the co-opt priced into its ORDC steps. ERCOT-79 found and fixed the detector (event-based detection for cycling classes; source-faithful, measured CEMS + EIA-930, validated 58h false-outage 1,904->0 MW/h, 0% genuine-outage over-correction) and the fix was ADOPTED (corrected campd-outages.csv installed). On the corrected fleet the keeper recipe (re-solved as keeper 2026-07-17-ercot79-corrected-outages) resolves the 2023 summer over-shoot ($1,068->$242, confirming ERCOT-78) but UN-CATCHES the real scarcity tail (2023 C3c 179->53 vs RT 181, Aug caught 71->25, 2025 tail 19->0) — the offer/scarcity calibration was tuned against the phantom-tightened fleet. DETERMINATION: NOT-YET (C3a/C3b/C3c fail on accurate data). OPEN LANE (successor): a full ERCOT offer-curve + ORDC/co-opt re-calibration against the corrected availability envelope, so the real scarcity re-forms on real fleet tightness. CROSS-ISO: the detector is shared — PJM's committed facility csv shows a stronger phantom signature and all six ISOs' unit-level extracts use it; each ISO is its own regenerate-and-re-audit lane. See results/calibration/FINDING-ercot79-phantom-outage-2026-07.md.
